title: The inbox's operator-word tooth judges only the inbox's own structural lines
intention: The inbox proof's 'Operator, not Akien' tooth judges only the lines the inbox itself writes as structure (headers and rules), never relayed notice, trouble or question text, so a record that names a path under /home/akien cannot red it.
why: Measured 2026-10-11 by the builder (trouble inbox-proof-reds-on-a-trouble-naming-an-inbox-path): test_operator_inbox.py::test_format_uses_operator_not_akien (~:389) counts every rendered line whose text contains 'INBOX' as structural, over LIVE gather_all() data. A live notice or trouble that names an operator_inbox path under /home/akien is such a line, so the tooth reds on content the inbox only relays. It feeds itself: sealing this proof emits a notice naming the proof's own path, and the next run reds on that notice. It held abcad52a407e at PROVEME.
traces_to: Law 8 (a proof must red on the defect it guards, not on relayed data), and memory proof-over-live-data-assert-invariants.
how: cairn/tools/operator_inbox/proofs/test_operator_inbox.py test_format_uses_operator_not_akien only: a line is structural when it starts (unstripped) with '--' or '==', or is unindented and contains 'INBOX'; indented relayed lines are not judged. No change to inbox.py.
falsifier: cairn/tools/operator_inbox/proofs/test_operator_inbox.py gains a tooth under PROVES {'0162736f42ed': {'1','2'}}: (1) format_inbox over data whose notices carry an indented line naming /home/akien/.../operator_inbox/... passes the operator-word check; (2) a structural header line reading 'AKIEN INBOX' (unindented) still fails it. Hollow: today's 'INBOX in line' check reds 1.

decisions.text: Its own ticket, not folded into abcad52a407e: the red is in a neighbouring tooth that predates abca, and abca re-crosses PROVEME after this one is PROVED. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09
Narrow the tooth to the inbox's own structural lines (the builder's proposal); the tooth's aim, the inbox's own words say Operator, is unchanged. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

The check is one helper in cairn/tools/operator_inbox/proofs/test_operator_inbox.py, _operator_word_reds(output) -> list of offending lines; test_format_uses_operator_not_akien asserts it returns [] over format_inbox(gather_all()). The build changes only the helper's structural test, from 'stripped line starts with -- or == or contains INBOX' to 'the line as rendered starts with -- or ==, or does not start with whitespace and contains INBOX'; a structural line with AKIEN in it is a red. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

Tooth 1's relayed line is a live trouble whose why names /home/akien/dev/src/cairn/cairn/tools/operator_inbox/proofs/test_operator_inbox.py, passed through format_inbox(dict(gather_all(), troubles={live:[...], live_count:1, total_count:1})); a trouble's why renders indented exactly as a notice does, and the trouble lane is the shape the measured red came through. The tooth first asserts the path rendered. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

The teeth are written and committed red-first at 8ae74a95 in cairn/tools/operator_inbox/proofs/test_operator_inbox.py: PROVES '0162736f42ed' {'1': test_an_indented_relayed_line_naming_an_inbox_path_passes_the_operator_word_check, '2': test_an_unindented_akien_inbox_header_still_fails_the_operator_word_check}. Measured before the build: tooth 1 red, tooth 2 green, and the live operator-word tooth red over the live inbox. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

The build writes only the proof file, which the tester's hollow reading skips as an instrument; the red-first run at 8ae74a95 over today's check IS the reading that reds clause 1, and the verdict cites it. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

The build is proofs-only by design (D10): it writes only cairn/tools/operator_inbox/proofs/test_operator_inbox.py, which hollow skips as the instrument (SKIP_INSTRUMENT). The rule that seals it is code, not a reading: cairn/devices/tester/hollow.py measure() (:1055-1071, ticket bf1cd5d79805, PROVED) — when no file was measured, every skip is the instrument or a record, at least one is the instrument, and no file went unwritten, it calls approval(ticket, skipped) (:712), which returns 'plan' when every skipped path is an element of the ticket's top-level writes_to list; the files are then sealed approved: plan instead of red 'measured nothing'. This ticket's writes_to is now exactly [that proof path], so the hollow reading seals {approved: plan}. The red-first run at 8ae74a95 remains the reading that reds clause 1. No code changes. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

No decompose berth is regenerated and there is no step to keep it in sync: hollow reads its file list from the standing decompose berth (hollow.writes_to -> chain_for_ticket(...)['decompose'], sub_problems[].writes_to) and its plan approval from the ticket's top-level writes_to (hollow.approval). Measured 2026-10-12: both already read exactly ['cairn/tools/operator_inbox/proofs/test_operator_inbox.py'], so they agree and the hollow run seals {approved: plan} as written. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

The FIXME->BUILDME crossing passes target 'BUILDME' and why='FIXME 1 settled by D12-D14; the proof stands committed, nothing to build'. actor is always 'cc'; there is no --actor or --why flag because there is no CLI verb.
